<a id="architecture"></a>

## Architecture

Doctrine: .agents/skills/pij-team/TENETS.md. ONE UNIT, no fan-out, but it is a CROSS-RUNTIME SEAM (Rust daemon ↔ TS extension) — the class that has bitten this repo repeatedly: both suites green, wire dead between them. RULE: make one side READ the other's definition or assert against one shared artifact; never restate the field name in two places, and only an end-to-end run proves the wire. Settled seam: PushedEvent gains the claim handle the ack path already requires (job_id or an explicit equivalent) — ADDITIVE field (design-change-additive tenet); the extension acks via the existing /v1/inbox/ack contract after a successful inject, and ONLY after (ack-after-render ordering is the contract, same discipline as s119's F4). The daemon must not announce a row whose consumer acked it; decide and STATE whether suppression is (a) the ack arriving first, or (b) an explicit consumer-claim — and name the race you are accepting either way. A failed inject must NOT ack (the body must remain deliverable) — that is ac-3's whole point. STOP-AND-ASK: any need to change uds can_deliver, s121's registration/migration files, or s122's rung selection.

<a id="fan-out"></a>

## Fan out

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| decision | &lt;solo-pm \| coders&gt; |
| rationale | &lt;Why. Rules: SOLO-PM when the work has no parallelizable seams or is small — the PM codes it itself, then runs the reviewer. CODERS when units below can proceed in parallel (or it is multi-phase): 1-n coders per wave, PM composes after each wave, reviewer after composition. The units table is the argument for this decision — if you cannot write independent unit rows with clean interfaces, the answer is solo-pm. Dispatch overhead counts: a unit cheaper than its own dispatch (spawn+canary+ack+review) is not a unit - fold it into a sibling.&gt; |

<a id="isolation"></a>

## Isolation

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| mode | worktree-per-coder |
| note | Default: each coder gets its own worktree, branching off the PM's plan branch; unit lands back onto the plan branch (PM merges — coders never merge). Shared-tree work is the retro-proven #1 hazard (staged sweeps, untrustworthy greens) — only choose it for trivially disjoint single-wave work, and then file-scoped `git add` only, never -A. REMEMBER: fences partition WRITE intent, not the build — a mid-refactor sibling can still break your compile, so waves must respect build dependencies, and a broken workspace build is a PM composition concern, not a coder's to fix cross-fence. |

<a id="composition"></a>

## Composition

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| composer | pm |
| steps | &lt;Composition is an explicit, separate step — the first-light pattern: everything already exists as tested parts; this is the wiring that makes them one system. Read order = each unit's service page / done report. Steps: merge unit branches in dependency order onto the plan branch → wire at the composition root → make `harness checks` green on the composed tree → run the integration proof. Known composition failure modes to check deliberately: mis-wiring (right parts, wrong plumbing), interface drift from this doc, envelope/schema drift between units, stale doc-comments across fence boundaries. RULE: composition is wiring, not building — if a unit needs INTERNAL rework at compose time, that is a defect in the contracts phase, not a composition task: stop, record it (harness observe + the skill EXPERIENCES.md), and have it ruled before touching the unit.&gt; |
| integration_proof | &lt;the named end-to-end evidence: integration test file(s) and/or a live run transcript captured as the plan's exit evidence&gt; |
